correctness.rationale: Let m>=2, d=m+1, positive a_i, b=min a_i. Uniqueness of the scalar root t in [1,d/2) follows from strict monotonicity of H(t)=t sum_i b²/(d a_i²-t b²), H(1)<=1 and H(d/2)>1. Coordinate-reflection symmetry and extremal widths give unique John ellipsoid with semiaxes (a_i,b). For Löwner set p_i=1/(d a_i²-t b²), r=1/(t b²), and use sum p_i=r, sum a_i²p_i=1 to prove K is inside L, with equality precisely when all cylinders saturate, the entire contact ridge. A two-orbit signed contact measure with weights (d-t)/d and t/d has zero mean and normalized covariance I/d, proving global Löwner optimality (not merely diagonal). Log-concave scalar product G_c(t) yields exact ratio sqrt(t prod_i(d-t/c_i)), strict aspect monotonicity and sharp [m^(m/2), d^(d/2)/2) range; upper approached only in divergent-radius limit. Independent numeric root/isotropic-moment checks for multiple m and radii corroborate the argument.
residual_risks: All radii positive, m>=2; upper ratio is unattained singular-radius limit.
